weeks.title: Learning from data: tasks, losses and generalisation
weeks.summary: Is week aap ML problems ko supervised/unsupervised aur regression/classification me classify karna, loss function se model ki galti naapna, aur training vs test error se overfitting pehchanna seekhoge.
concepts: **Machine learning ka setup**: data D = {(x₁, y₁), …, (xₙ, yₙ)}, jahan xᵢ ∈ ℝᵈ ek feature vector hai aur yᵢ label. Hum ek function family (model class) choose karte hain, jaise f(x) = wᵀx + b, aur data se aise parameters dhoondhte hain jo naye, unseen x par bhi achha predict karein. Asli goal training data yaad karna nahi, **generalise** karna hai.

**Supervised vs unsupervised**: supervised learning me har x ke saath label y diya hota hai (house price, spam/not-spam). Unsupervised me sirf x hote hain aur hum structure dhoondhte hain: clustering (customer segments), dimensionality reduction (PCA), density estimation. Label hai ya nahi, yahi pehla sawaal hai.

**Regression vs classification**: label continuous real number ho (price, temperature, delivery time) to regression; label ek finite set se ho ({spam, not spam}, {0, 1, …, 9}) to classification. Output ka type decide karta hai, input ka type nahi.

**Loss function** ℓ(ŷ, y) batata hai ki ek prediction kitni galat hai. Regression me squared loss (ŷ − y)² aur absolute loss |ŷ − y| common hain; classification me 0-1 loss (galat = 1, sahi = 0) aur probabilistic models ke liye cross-entropy −[y ln p + (1 − y) ln(1 − p)]. Training ka matlab hai **empirical risk** (1/n) Σ ℓ(f(xᵢ), yᵢ) ko minimise karna.

**Squared vs absolute loss**: squared loss bade errors ko zyada punish karta hai, isliye outliers ka asar bada hota hai. Ek constant predictor c ke liye Σ(yᵢ − c)² ka minimiser **mean** hai aur Σ|yᵢ − c| ka minimiser **median**. Isliye absolute loss outliers ke against zyada robust hai.

**Training, validation aur test split**: model ko training set par fit karo, hyperparameters (polynomial degree, regularisation strength) validation set par choose karo, aur test set ko sirf end me ek baar final estimate ke liye use karo. Test set par model choose kiya to wo estimate optimistic (biased) ho jaata hai.

**Overfitting aur underfitting**: bahut simple model training aur test dono par high error deta hai (underfitting, high bias). Bahut flexible model training error ko lagbhag zero kar deta hai par test error badh jaata hai (overfitting, high variance), kyunki wo noise bhi yaad kar leta hai. Model complexity badhane par training error ghatta hai, test error pehle ghatkar phir badhta hai (U-shape).

**Interpolation ka trap**: n points jinke x alag-alag hain, unhe degree n − 1 polynomial exactly pass kar sakta hai, yaani training error 0. Ye achha model hone ka saboot nahi hai; zero training error ke saath aksar test error sabse kharab hota hai.

example.problem: Ek fictional delivery startup 4 orders ka delivery time (minutes) predict karta hai. Actual y = (30, 42, 25, 50), model ke predictions ŷ = (28, 45, 25, 44). Mean squared error (MSE) aur mean absolute error (MAE) nikalo, aur batao kaunsa error outlier jaisi badi galti ko zyada weight deta hai.
steps: Sabse badi galti 6 ka MSE me contribution 36/49 ≈ 73% hai, jabki MAE me sirf 6/11 ≈ 55%.
Answer: **MSE = 12.25, MAE = 2.75**; squared loss badi galtiyon ko zyada weight deta hai.

mistakes: Test set par baar-baar models compare karke best choose karna. Tab test error ek honest estimate nahi rehta. Model selection ke liye alag validation set (ya cross-validation) rakho.
Zero training error ko best model maan lena. Flexible model noise ko bhi fit kar leta hai; hamesha validation/test error dekho.
Problem ko input ke type se regression/classification bolna. Decide output (label) ka type karta hai: numeric continuous label = regression, category = classification.
revision: Supervised: (x, y) pairs; unsupervised: sirf x.
Regression: continuous label; classification: discrete label.
Squared loss ka best constant = mean; absolute loss ka = median.
Overfitting: training error low, test error high.
Validation se model choose karo, test sirf final report ke liye.

questions.question: Ek fictional online store ke paas customers ki purchase history hai, par koi label nahi. Wo customers ko similar buying behaviour wale groups me baantna chahta hai. Ye kis type ka ML problem hai?
questions.explanation: Data me koi label y nahi hai aur goal groups (structure) dhoondhna hai, isliye ye unsupervised clustering hai. Option B tempting hai kyunki output 'group' ek category lagti hai, par classification ke liye training me har customer ka sahi group pehle se pata hona chahiye, jo yahan nahi hai.

questions.question: Ek regression model ke liye actual values y = (3, 5, 2, 8) aur predictions ŷ = (2.5, 5, 4, 7) hain. Mean squared error (MSE) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Errors: 0.5, 0, −2, 1. Squares: 0.25, 0, 4, 1, sum = 5.25. MSE = 5.25 / 4 = 1.3125. Option B (0.875) MAE hai (absolute errors ka mean), option C (5.25) sum of squared errors hai jisme n se divide karna bhool gaye, aur option D RMSE = √1.3125 hai.

questions.question: Teen polynomial regression models ke errors (MSE) ye hain. Degree 1: train 4.1, validation 4.3. Degree 3: train 1.2, validation 1.5. Degree 9: train 0.05, validation 6.8. Kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Degree 9 best hai kyunki uska training error sabse kam hai
Degree 3 choose karna chahiye; degree 9 overfit kar raha hai
Degree 1 overfit kar raha hai kyunki uske dono errors close hain
Final model choose karne ke liye test set par teeno ka error compare karna chahiye
questions.explanation: Model selection validation error se hota hai: degree 3 ka validation error (1.5) sabse kam hai. Degree 9 ka training error 0.05 par validation 6.8 hai, jo overfitting ka classic sign hai, isliye option A ka trap training error par bharosa karna hai. Degree 1 underfit (high bias) hai, overfit nahi. Option D galat hai kyunki test set par choose karne se final estimate biased ho jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek binary classifier do examples par probability p = P(y = 1) deta hai: pehle example ka y = 1 aur p = 0.8, doosre ka y = 0 aur p = 0.3. Natural log use karke average cross-entropy loss kya hai?
questions.explanation: Loss = −[y ln p + (1 − y) ln(1 − p)]. Pehla: −ln 0.8 = 0.2231. Doosra (y = 0): −ln(1 − 0.3) = −ln 0.7 = 0.3567. Average = (0.2231 + 0.3567)/2 = 0.2899. Option B me doosre example ke liye −ln 0.3 le liya (y = 0 hone par 1 − p lena tha), option A sum hai average nahi, aur option C me log base 10 use ho gaya.

questions.question: Training data me 6 points hain jinke x values sab alag hain. Kis minimum degree ka polynomial in sab points se exactly guzar sakta hai (training MSE = 0, chahe y kuch bhi ho)?
questions.explanation: Degree k polynomial me k + 1 coefficients hote hain. 6 alag x par 6 equations hain, to 6 unknowns chahiye: k + 1 = 6, k = 5 (Vandermonde system invertible hai jab x alag hon). Option A ka trap points ki count ko hi degree maan lena hai. Ye bhi yaad rakho: aisa zero training error aksar overfitting hota hai.

questions.question: Data {1, 2, 3, 10} ke liye ek constant predictor ŷ = c choose karna hai. Squared loss Σ(yᵢ − c)² aur absolute loss Σ|yᵢ − c| ko minimise karne wale c kya hain?
options: Squared: c = 4; absolute: [2, 3] me koi bhi c
questions.explanation: Squared loss ka minimiser mean hai: (1 + 2 + 3 + 10)/4 = 4 (derivative −2Σ(yᵢ − c) = 0). Absolute loss ka minimiser median hai; even count me 2 aur 3 ke beech har c same loss 10 deta hai (c = 2, 2.5, 3 sab par sum = 10, jabki c = 4 par 12). Option D tempting hai kyunki median ko 2.5 padhaya jaata hai, par absolute loss ke liye poora interval [2, 3] optimal hai. Option B mean/median ulte kar deta hai; outlier 10 mean ko kheenchta hai, median ko nahi.

questions.question: Ek fictional weather app past records (humidity, wind speed, aaj ka temperature aur us din ke baad wale din ka asli maximum temperature in °C) se kal ka maximum temperature predict karna chahta hai. Ye kis type ka ML problem hai?
questions.explanation: Har record ke saath sahi answer (agle din ka temperature) diya hai, to ye supervised hai, aur label ek continuous real number (°C) hai, to regression. Option B tempting hai kyunki weather ko aksar sunny/rainy jaisi categories me socha jaata hai, par yahan output ek number hai, category nahi. Options A aur D unsupervised hain, jabki yahan label maujood hai.

questions.question: Ek model ke liye actual values y = (10, 12, 8, 6) aur predictions ŷ = (11, 10, 8, 9) hain. Mean absolute error (MAE) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Errors y − ŷ: −1, 2, 0, −3. Absolute errors 1, 2, 0, 3, sum = 6, MAE = 6/4 = 1.5. Option B (3.5) MSE hai (squares 1, 4, 0, 9 ka mean), option C (6) sum hai jisme n = 4 se divide karna bhool gaye, aur option D RMSE = √3.5 hai.

questions.question: Train / validation / test split me test set ka sahi use kya hai?
options: Har epoch ke baad learning rate tune karne ke liye
Polynomial degree choose karne ke liye
Training set ke saath milakar model fit karne ke liye
Model final hone ke baad ek baar error report karne ke liye
questions.explanation: Test set sirf end me ek baar use hota hai, jab saari choices fix ho chuki hon, taaki error ka honest (unbiased) estimate mile. Options A aur B hyperparameter choices hain, jo validation set ka kaam hai; test set par ye karne se final estimate optimistic ho jaata hai. Option C me test data training me chala jaata hai, phir wo unseen data ka estimate nahi de sakta.

questions.question: Ek binary classifier 5 examples par p = P(y = 1) deta hai: p = (0.7, 0.4, 0.9, 0.2, 0.6) aur sahi labels y = (1, 1, 0, 0, 1). Threshold 0.5 par predict karke average 0-1 loss (empirical risk) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Threshold 0.5 par predictions: 1, 0, 1, 0, 1. Galtiyan: example 2 (y = 1 par 0 predict) aur example 3 (y = 0 par 1 predict), yaani 2 galat. Average 0-1 loss = 2/5 = 0.4. Option A (0.6) accuracy hai, loss nahi. Option C sirf ek galti ginta hai; example 3 ka p = 0.9 confident lagta hai par label 0 hai, to wo bhi galat hai. Option D galtiyon ki count hai, n se divide nahi kiya.

questions.question: Polynomial regression me degree (model complexity) dheere-dheere badhate jaane par training error aur test error typically kaise badalte hain?
options: Training error ghatta hai; test error ghatkar phir badhta hai
Dono errors complexity ke saath lagatar ghatte rehte hain
Training error badhta hai; test error lagatar ghatta rehta hai
Dono pehle ghatte hain, phir dono ek saath badhne lagte hain
questions.explanation: Zyada flexible model training data ko aur achhe se fit karta hai, isliye training error lagatar ghatta hai. Test error pehle ghatta hai (underfitting kam hoti hai) aur phir badhta hai jab model noise yaad karne lagta hai (overfitting): U-shape. Option B ka trap ye maanna hai ki training error ki tarah test error bhi sudharta rahega. Option D galat hai kyunki training error complexity ke saath badhta nahi.

questions.question: Data {1, 3, 5, 7, 34} ke liye constant predictor ŷ = c. Squared loss ka best c₁ aur absolute loss ka best c₂ nikalo. Total absolute loss Σ|yᵢ − c| c = c₁ par, c = c₂ ke comparison me kitna zyada hai?
questions.explanation: Squared loss ka minimiser mean: (1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 34)/5 = 10. Absolute loss ka minimiser median: 5. c = 10 par Σ|yᵢ − c| = 9 + 7 + 5 + 3 + 24 = 48; c = 5 par = 4 + 2 + 0 + 2 + 29 = 37. Farak = 11. Option A mean aur median ulte kar deta hai. Option B maanta hai dono c same absolute loss denge, jo galat hai kyunki median hi absolute loss ka unique best yahan hai. Option C ka trap c₁ − c₂ = 5 ko loss ka farak samajhna hai. Outlier 34 mean ko kheench leta hai, median ko nahi.

questions.question: Do models f₁(x) = 2x + 1 aur f₂(x) = 3x − 1 ko validation points (1, 3.5), (2, 4.5), (3, 8) par compare karna hai. Validation MSE aur MAE ke hisaab se kya sahi hai?
options: MSE aur MAE dono me f₁ clearly better hai
MSE me f₁ better (0.5 vs 0.8333); MAE me tie (0.6667)
MSE me f₂ better (0.5 vs 0.8333); MAE me f₁ better
MSE aur MAE dono me f₂ better, ek prediction exact hai
questions.explanation: f₁ ke predictions 3, 5, 7, errors 0.5, −0.5, 1: MSE = (0.25 + 0.25 + 1)/3 = 0.5, MAE = 2/3 = 0.6667. f₂ ke predictions 2, 5, 8, errors 1.5, −0.5, 0: MSE = (2.25 + 0.25 + 0)/3 = 0.8333, MAE = 2/3 = 0.6667. Squared loss f₂ ki ek badi galti (1.5) ko zyada punish karta hai, isliye MSE f₁ ko chunta hai, jabki MAE dono ko barabar maanta hai. Option D ka trap ek exact prediction ko dekhkar model ko better maan lena hai; option A MAE ke tie ko miss karta hai.

questions.question: Ek classifier 3 examples par p = P(y = 1) deta hai: (y = 1, p = 0.9), (y = 0, p = 0.1), (y = 1, p = 0.1). Natural log ke saath average cross-entropy loss kya hai?
questions.explanation: Loss = −[y ln p + (1 − y) ln(1 − p)]. Pehla: −ln 0.9 = 0.1054. Doosra (y = 0): −ln(1 − 0.1) = −ln 0.9 = 0.1054. Teesra: −ln 0.1 = 2.3026. Average = 2.5133/3 = 0.8378. Option B sirf pehle do achhe examples ka loss hai; teesra confident-but-wrong example hi loss ko dominate karta hai. Option C sum hai average nahi, aur option D me log base 10 use ho gaya.

questions.question: 50 points (sabke x alag) ko 60% train, 20% validation aur 20% test me baanta. Sirf training set par fit karke training MSE = 0 (chahe y kuch bhi ho) dene wale polynomial ki minimum degree kya hai, aur validation error ke baare me kya umeed karni chahiye?
options: Degree 30; validation error bhi 0 hi hoga
Degree 29; validation error aksar high hoga
Degree 49; test error sabse kam hoga
questions.explanation: Training set = 60% of 50 = 30 points. 30 alag x ko exactly fit karne ke liye 30 coefficients chahiye, yaani degree 29. Aisa interpolating polynomial noise bhi fit karta hai, isliye validation error aksar bahut kharab hota hai. Option A points ki count ko degree maan leta hai (degree 30 me 31 coefficients). Option B train + validation (40 points) par ginta hai, aur option D saare 50 points par; dono me zero training error ko achha model samajhne ka trap bhi hai.

weeks.title: Calculus toolkit: gradients, chain rule and Taylor approximations
weeks.summary: Is week aap partial derivatives aur gradient nikalna, loss function par chain rule lagana, aur first/second-order Taylor approximation se function ko locally approximate karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Derivative as local slope**: f′(a) = lim (f(a + h) − f(a))/h jab h → 0. ML me iska practical matlab: parameter ko thoda sa h badhao to loss lagbhag f′(a)·h badhega. Isi sensitivity se training chalti hai.
**Partial derivative**: f(x, y) me ∂f/∂x nikalte waqt y ko constant maano. Jaise f = x²y + 3y² ke liye ∂f/∂x = 2xy aur ∂f/∂y = x² + 6y. Har parameter ki apni sensitivity hoti hai.

**Gradient** ∇f = (∂f/∂x₁, …, ∂f/∂x_d) ek vector hai jo steepest increase ki direction batata hai. Unit vector u ki direction me rate of change (directional derivative) = ∇f · u, jo maximum |∇f| hota hai jab u gradient ke parallel ho. Isliye gradient descent −∇f ki direction me chalta hai.

**Chain rule**: agar L = g(h(w)), to dL/dw = g′(h(w)) · h′(w). Squared loss L = (wx − y)² ke liye dL/dw = 2(wx − y) · x. Multivariable case me ∂L/∂wⱼ = Σₖ (∂L/∂zₖ)(∂zₖ/∂wⱼ); neural networks ka backpropagation isi ka systematic use hai.
**Linear (first-order) approximation**: f(a + Δ) ≈ f(a) + ∇f(a) · Δ. Ye point a par tangent plane hai. Δ chhota ho to error Δ ke square jitna chhota hota hai.

**Second-order Taylor approximation**: f(a + Δ) ≈ f(a) + ∇f(a) · Δ + ½ Δᵀ H Δ, jahan H Hessian matrix hai (Hᵢⱼ = ∂²f/∂xᵢ∂xⱼ). Curvature ki ye information Newton's method aur minima/maxima ki pehchaan (week 7) me kaam aati hai.

**Useful derivatives**: d/dx eˣ = eˣ, d/dx ln x = 1/x, sigmoid σ(z) = 1/(1 + e⁻ᶻ) ke liye σ′(z) = σ(z)(1 − σ(z)). Vector form me ∇(aᵀx) = a aur ∇(xᵀAx) = (A + Aᵀ)x, jo A symmetric ho to 2Ax ban jaata hai.

example.problem: Ek single-feature model ŷ = wx + b aur ek training example (x = 2, y = 7) ke liye squared loss L(w, b) = (wx + b − y)² hai. w = 1, b = 1 par gradient ∇L = (∂L/∂w, ∂L/∂b) nikalo aur batao ki loss kam karne ke liye w ko badhana chahiye ya ghatana.
steps: Gradient negative hai, matlab w badhane par L ghatega; gradient descent w ← w − η(−16) w ko badhata hai.
Answer: **∇L = (−16, −8)**; w aur b dono ko badhana chahiye.
example.code:
x, y = 2, 7
w, b = 1.0, 1.0
r = w * x + b - y
grad_w = 2 * r * x
grad_b = 2 * r
print(grad_w, grad_b)   # -16.0 -8.0

mistakes: Chain rule me inner derivative bhool jaana: (wx − y)² ka w-derivative 2(wx − y) nahi, 2(wx − y)·x hai.
Second-order Taylor me ½ factor chhod dena, ya cross term ∂²f/∂x∂y ko sirf ek baar ginna. ΔᵀHΔ me cross term 2·Hₓᵧ·Δx·Δy aata hai.
Gradient ko descent direction samajhna. ∇f increase ki direction hai; minimise karne ke liye −∇f lo.
revision: ∇f = vector of partial derivatives; ∇f · u = directional derivative.
σ′(z) = σ(z)(1 − σ(z)); ∇(xᵀAx) = 2Ax for symmetric A.

questions.question: f(x) = x³ − 4x ke liye f′(2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 3x² − 4, to f′(2) = 12 − 4 = 8. Option C (12) me sirf 3x² ka part liya, −4 bhool gaye. Option A (0) f(2) = 8 − 8 hai, derivative nahi.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x²y + 3y² ka gradient point (1, 2) par kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∂f/∂x = 2xy = 2·1·2 = 4. ∂f/∂y = x² + 6y = 1 + 12 = 13. Gradient (4, 13). Option B me 3y² ka derivative 3y le liya (power rule me 2 ka factor chhoot gaya), option C me x² wala term bhool gaye, aur option A me ∂f/∂x ke liye y ki jagah 1 rakh diya.

questions.question: Ek example (x = 2, y = 3) par loss L(w) = (wx − y)² hai. w = 1 par dL/dw kya hai?
questions.explanation: Chain rule: dL/dw = 2(wx − y)·x = 2(2 − 3)·2 = −4. Option B (−2) me inner derivative x = 2 bhool gaye. Option C sign ulta hai, jo tab hota hai jab residual ko (y − wx) likhkar inner derivative ka minus chhod dete ho.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x²y ka point (2, 1) par linear approximation use karke f(2.1, 0.95) ka estimate kya hai?
questions.explanation: f(2, 1) = 4, ∇f = (2xy, x²) = (4, 4). Δ = (0.1, −0.05). Estimate = 4 + 4(0.1) + 4(−0.05) = 4 + 0.4 − 0.2 = 4.2. Option B (4.1895) exact value hai, linear approximation nahi. Option A me Δy ka sign + le liya, aur option D me y-direction ka change ignore kar diya.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x² + 2y² ka point (1, 1) par unit vector u = (0.6, 0.8) ki direction me directional derivative kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∇f = (2x, 4y) = (2, 4). Directional derivative = ∇f · u = 2(0.6) + 4(0.8) = 1.2 + 3.2 = 4.4. Option B (√20) |∇f| hai, yaani maximum possible rate, jo sirf gradient ki direction me milta hai. Option A me gradient ki jagah f ke coefficients (1, 2) use hue: 0.6 + 1.6 = 2.2. Option D gradient components ka sum hai.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x³ + xy² ka point (1, 1) par second-order Taylor approximation use karke f(1.1, 0.9) ka estimate kya hai?
questions.explanation: f(1, 1) = 2. ∇f = (3x² + y², 2xy) = (4, 2). Hessian H = [[6x, 2y], [2y, 2x]] = [[6, 2], [2, 2]]. Δ = (0.1, −0.1). Linear part: 2 + 0.4 − 0.2 = 2.2. ΔᵀHΔ = 6(0.01) + 2·2(0.1)(−0.1) + 2(0.01) = 0.06 − 0.04 + 0.02 = 0.04, aur ½ · 0.04 = 0.02. Estimate 2.22 (exact value 2.222). Option A sirf linear approximation hai, option C me ½ bhool gaye, aur option D me cross term ka sign + le liya.

questions.question: f(x) = 3x² + ln x ke liye f′(1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 6x + 1/x, to f′(1) = 6 + 1 = 7. Option A ln x ka derivative 1/x bhool jaata hai, option C f(1) = 3 hai (derivative nahi, function ki value), aur option D sirf ln x wala hissa hai.

questions.question: Sigmoid σ(z) = 1/(1 + e⁻ᶻ) ka derivative z = 0 par kya hai?
questions.explanation: σ′(z) = σ(z)(1 − σ(z)). z = 0 par σ(0) = 0.5, to σ′(0) = 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25. Option A σ(0) khud hai, derivative nahi. Option B slope ko 1 maan leta hai, aur option C galat hai kyunki z = 0 par sigmoid sabse steep hota hai, flat nahi.

questions.question: f(x, y) = 3x²y + y³ ke liye point (1, 2) par ∂f/∂y kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∂f/∂y nikalte waqt x constant: ∂f/∂y = 3x² + 3y². (1, 2) par 3 + 12 = 15. Option B ∂f/∂x = 6xy = 12 hai (galat variable), option C f(1, 2) = 6 + 8 = 14 hai, aur option D y³ ka term bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: A = [[1, 2], [0, 3]] (symmetric nahi) aur f(x) = xᵀAx. Point x = (1, 1) par ∇f kya hai?
questions.explanation: General rule: ∇(xᵀAx) = (A + Aᵀ)x. A + Aᵀ = [[2, 2], [2, 6]], to ∇f = (2 + 2, 2 + 6) = (4, 8). Check: f = x₁² + 2x₁x₂ + 3x₂², ∂f/∂x₁ = 2x₁ + 2x₂ = 4, ∂f/∂x₂ = 2x₁ + 6x₂ = 8. Option A 2Ax = (6, 6) hai, jo sirf symmetric A ke liye sahi formula hai; yahi main trap hai. Option B Ax aur option D Aᵀx hai.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x² + 3y ke liye point (2, 1) par kis unit direction me f sabse tezi se badhta hai, aur wo maximum rate kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∇f = (2x, 3) = (4, 3) at (2, 1). Steepest increase gradient ki direction me hai: unit vector (4, 3)/5 = (0.8, 0.6), aur rate = |∇f| = √(16 + 9) = 5. Option A sirf x-direction ka partial derivative hai. Option C components ka sum 7 leta hai aur direction unit vector nahi hai. Option D |∇f|² = 25 deta hai, square root bhool gaye.

questions.question: Model ŷ = σ(wx) aur loss L = (ŷ − y)² hai. Ek example x = 2, y = 1 par w = 0 par dL/dw kya hai?
questions.explanation: Chain rule: dL/dw = 2(ŷ − y) · σ′(wx) · x. w = 0 par z = 0, ŷ = σ(0) = 0.5, σ′(0) = 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25. To dL/dw = 2(−0.5)(0.25)(2) = −0.5. Option B sigmoid ka derivative σ′ wala factor chhod deta hai. Option D σ′ ki jagah σ = 0.5 lagata hai. Option C inner derivative d(wx)/dw = x = 2 bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: f(x) = xᵀAx + bᵀx, jahan A = [[2, 1], [1, 3]] (symmetric) aur b = (1, −2). Point x = (1, 1) par unit vector u = (0.6, −0.8) ki direction me directional derivative kya hai?
questions.explanation: A symmetric hai, to ∇f = 2Ax + b. Ax = (3, 4), 2Ax = (6, 8), ∇f = (7, 6). Directional derivative = ∇f · u = 7(0.6) + 6(−0.8) = 4.2 − 4.8 = −0.6. Option A me 2Ax ki jagah Ax liya gaya (∇f = (4, 2)), option B b ko chhod deta hai (∇f = (6, 8)), aur option C u ke doosre component ka minus sign bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: ln x ka point x = 1 par second-order Taylor approximation use karke ln(1.2) ka estimate kya hai?
questions.explanation: f(1) = 0, f′(x) = 1/x ⇒ f′(1) = 1, f″(x) = −1/x² ⇒ f″(1) = −1. ln(1 + Δ) ≈ Δ − ½Δ², Δ = 0.2: 0.2 − 0.02 = 0.18 (asli ln 1.2 ≈ 0.1823). Option A sirf first-order (linear) approximation hai. Option B second derivative ka sign galat leta hai (+0.02). Option D ½ factor bhool jaata hai (0.2 − 0.04).

questions.question: Ek chhota two-step model: h = w₁x, ŷ = w₂h, loss L = (ŷ − y)². Example x = 1, y = 5 aur current w₁ = 2, w₂ = 1. Gradient (∂L/∂w₁, ∂L/∂w₂) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Forward: h = 2, ŷ = 2, ∂L/∂ŷ = 2(ŷ − y) = −6. Chain rule: ∂L/∂w₂ = (∂L/∂ŷ) · h = −6 × 2 = −12, aur ∂L/∂w₁ = (∂L/∂ŷ) · w₂ · x = −6 × 1 × 1 = −6. Option C dono components ulte kar deta hai. Option A ∂L/∂w₂ me h ki jagah x lagata hai. Option D squared loss ke derivative ka factor 2 bhool jaata hai.

weeks.title: Least squares as projection onto the column space
weeks.summary: Is week aap linear regression ko Ax ≈ b ke roop me likhna, normal equations AᵀAx̂ = Aᵀb se best fit nikalna, aur use column space par orthogonal projection ki tarah samajhna seekhoge.
concepts: **Regression as a linear system**: n examples aur d features ho to design matrix A (n × d) banao, har row ek example, aur agar intercept chahiye to pehla column saare 1 ka. Model ŷ = Ax. Usually n > d hota hai (zyada equations, kam unknowns), isliye Ax = b ka exact solution aam taur par exist nahi karta.

**Column space** C(A) = {Ax : x ∈ ℝᵈ}, yaani A ke columns ke saare linear combinations. Ax = b solvable hai tabhi jab b ∈ C(A). Jab b bahar ho, hum C(A) ka wo point p = Ax̂ dhoondhte hain jo b ke sabse kareeb ho.

**Least squares objective**: x̂ = argmin ‖Ax − b‖² = argmin Σ (aᵢᵀx − bᵢ)². Gradient 2Aᵀ(Ax − b) ko zero rakhne par **normal equations** milte hain: AᵀA x̂ = Aᵀb. Agar A ke columns linearly independent hain to AᵀA invertible hai aur x̂ = (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀb unique hai.

**Geometry: orthogonal projection**: best fit p = Ax̂ wo point hai jahan error e = b − p column space ke har vector se perpendicular ho: Aᵀe = 0. Normal equations isi condition ka algebraic roop hain. Projection matrix P = A(AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ, aur P² = P, Pᵀ = P.
**Projection onto a single line**: vector a ki direction me b ka projection p = (aᵀb / aᵀa) · a. Denominator aᵀa = ‖a‖² hai, ‖a‖ nahi. Ye d = 1 wala special case hai.

**Intercept ka asar**: column of ones hone se Aᵀe = 0 ki pehli equation kehti hai Σeᵢ = 0, yaani residuals ka sum zero, aur fitted line (x̄, ȳ) se guzarti hai. Bina intercept ke (line origin se forced) ye guarantee nahi milti.

**Rank deficiency**: agar ek feature doosre ka multiple hai (jaise height cm me aur inches me dono), to A ke columns dependent hain, AᵀA singular hai, aur x̂ unique nahi. Projection p phir bhi unique hota hai; sirf coefficients ka split ambiguous hai. Practice me duplicate feature hatao ya regularisation (ridge) use karo.

example.problem: Ek fictional shop ka ad spend x (lakh ₹) aur sales y (lakh ₹): (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 5), (4, 6). Line ŷ = c + mx ko least squares se fit karo aur check karo ki residuals column space ke orthogonal hain.
example.code:
def lstsq_line(xs, ys):
    n = len(xs)
    sx, sy = sum(xs), sum(ys)
    sxx = sum(x * x for x in xs)
    sxy = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(xs, ys))
    d = n * sxx - sx * sx
    c = (sxx * sy - sx * sxy) / d
    m = (n * sxy - sx * sy) / d
    return c, m

print(lstsq_line([1, 2, 3, 4], [2, 3, 5, 6]))   # (0.5, 1.4)

mistakes: AᵀA x̂ = Aᵀb ki jagah Ax̂ = b ko kisi bhi tarah solve karne ki koshish, jaise sirf pehli d rows le kar. Wo baaki equations ko ignore karta hai aur error minimise nahi karta.
Line par projection me aᵀb ko ‖a‖ se divide karna. Sahi formula p = (aᵀb / ‖a‖²)·a hai; unit vector u ho tabhi p = (uᵀb)u.
Intercept column bhool jaana. Bina column of ones ke fit origin se guzarne ko majboor hota hai aur residuals ka sum zero nahi rehta.
revision: Error e = b − Ax̂ satisfies Aᵀe = 0.
Dependent columns ⇒ AᵀA singular, x̂ unique nahi.

questions.question: A = [[1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]] (3 × 2). Kis b ke liye Ax = b ka exact solution exist karta hai?
questions.explanation: Ax = (x₁, x₂, x₁ + x₂), to column space me har vector ka teesra component pehle do ka sum hai. (2, 1, 3) me 2 + 1 = 3 ✓, x = (2, 1). Option A me 1 + 2 = 3 ≠ 4. Option D tempting hai kyunki usme bhi koi do components milkar teesra banate hain (1 + 2 = 3), par condition specifically b₃ = b₁ + b₂ hai.

questions.question: A (n × d, n > d, independent columns) ke liye ‖Ax − b‖² ko minimise karne wala x̂ kis equation ko satisfy karta hai?
questions.explanation: Gradient 2Aᵀ(Ax − b) = 0 se AᵀA x̂ = Aᵀb milta hai. Option D me dimensions hi match nahi karte: AᵀA x̂ d-dimensional hai jabki b n-dimensional. Option B me AAᵀ (n × n) aata hai jo x̂ (d entries) par lag hi nahi sakta. Har option ka shape check karna sabse tez filter hai.

questions.question: Points (0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 6), (3, 5) par line ŷ = c + mx ka least squares fit kya hai?
questions.explanation: Σx = 6, Σx² = 14, Σy = 15, Σxy = 0 + 3 + 12 + 15 = 30. Normal equations: 4c + 6m = 15, 6c + 14m = 30 ⇒ m = 1.5, c = 1.5. Option A pehle aur aakhri point ko jodne wali line hai (slope 4/3), jo baaki points ko ignore karti hai. Option B intercept ke bina fit hai (m = 30/14), aur option D sirf mean ȳ hai.

questions.question: b = (3, 0, 3) ka vector a = (1, 2, 2) ki line par orthogonal projection kya hai?
questions.explanation: aᵀb = 3 + 0 + 6 = 9, aᵀa = 1 + 4 + 4 = 9, to p = (9/9)·a = (1, 2, 2). Option A me ‖a‖ = 3 se divide kiya (‖a‖² se karna tha), option B me divide hi nahi kiya. Option C error vector e = b − p hai; check: aᵀe = 2 − 4 + 2 = 0.

questions.question: Ek fictional housing dataset me 'area in m²' aur 'area in ft²' dono features hain (ft² = 10.764 × m²), saath me intercept column. Least squares ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: AᵀA singular hai; fitted values Ax̂ unique hain par coefficients x̂ unique nahi
AᵀA invertible hai kyunki dono columns ke numbers alag hain
Koi least squares solution exist hi nahi karta
Fitted values bhi unique nahi hain, isliye predictions bharose layak nahi
questions.explanation: Ek column doosre ka exact multiple hai, to columns linearly dependent hain, rank(A) < d, aur AᵀA singular hai. Phir bhi b ka C(A) par projection p unique hai; sirf do dependent features ke beech weight ka split ambiguous hai (infinitely many x̂). Option B ka trap ye sochna hai ki alag numbers ka matlab independence hai. Option D galat hai kyunki projection hamesha unique hota hai.

questions.question: A = [[1, 0], [1, 1], [1, 2]] aur b = (1, 5, 3). Least squares solution x̂ aur minimum squared error ‖b − Ax̂‖² kya hain?
questions.explanation: AᵀA = [[3, 3], [3, 5]], Aᵀb = (9, 11). 3x₁ + 3x₂ = 9 aur 3x₁ + 5x₂ = 11 ⇒ x₂ = 1, x₁ = 2. p = Ax̂ = (2, 3, 4), e = (−1, 2, −1), ‖e‖² = 6, aur Aᵀe = (0, 0) ✓. Option B pehli do equations ko exactly solve karta hai (x₁ = 1, x₁ + x₂ = 5), jisse teesri row ka error 36 ho jaata hai. Option A sirf mean (slope 0) fit hai, aur option D me intercept aur slope swap ho gaye.

questions.question: Independent columns wali A ke liye projection matrix P = A(AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ ke baare me kya hamesha sahi hai?
options: Har b ke liye Pb = b
questions.explanation: Projection do baar karne se kuch nahi badalta (P² = P), aur orthogonal projection symmetric hota hai (Pᵀ = P). Options A, B aur D tabhi sahi hote jab column space poora space ho; n > d par C(A) chhota subspace hai, to P singular hai aur column space ke bahar wale b ko Pb badal deta hai.

questions.question: Ek fictional dataset me 50 houses hain, har ek ke 3 features, aur model me intercept bhi hai. Least squares ke liye design matrix A ka size kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Har row ek example (50 rows), aur columns = intercept ka ones column + 3 features = 4. To A 50 × 4 hai. Option B intercept column bhool jaata hai. Options C aur D rows aur columns ulte kar dete hain.

questions.question: Intercept wale least squares line fit ke residuals eᵢ = yᵢ − ŷᵢ ke baare me kya hamesha sahi hai?
options: Residuals ka sum zero hota hai
Residuals ka sum ȳ ke barabar hota hai
questions.explanation: Normal equations Aᵀe = 0 me ones column wali equation kehti hai Σeᵢ = 0. Option A tabhi hota jab saare points exactly line par hon. Option C galat hai kyunki sum zero hone ke liye positive aur negative dono residuals chahiye. Option D me sum ko ȳ se jod diya; line (x̄, ȳ) se guzarti hai, par residuals ka sum 0 hai.

questions.question: b = (2, 4) ka vector a = (3, 1) ki line par orthogonal projection kya hai?
questions.explanation: p = (aᵀb / aᵀa) a. aᵀb = 6 + 4 = 10, aᵀa = 9 + 1 = 10, to p = 1 · (3, 1) = (3, 1). Option A denominator me ‖a‖ = √10 leta hai, ‖a‖² nahi. Option B ulta projection hai (a ka b ki line par). Option C b ko hi answer maan leta hai, jabki b line par nahi hai.

questions.question: Bina intercept wali line ŷ = mx (origin se forced) ko points (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 7) par least squares se fit kiya. m kya hai?
questions.explanation: A ek column (1, 2, 3) hai, to m = Σxᵢyᵢ / Σxᵢ² = (2 + 6 + 21)/(1 + 4 + 9) = 29/14 ≈ 2.0714. Option A ȳ/x̄ = 4/2 hai, jo least squares nahi. Option B intercept wali line ka slope hai (Sxy/Sxx = 5/2), jo is model me allowed nahi. Option D fraction ulta kar deta hai (14/29).

questions.question: A = [[1, 0], [1, 1], [1, −1]] aur b = (2, 5, 2). Least squares solution x̂ aur residual e = b − Ax̂ kya hain?
questions.explanation: A ke columns orthogonal hain, to AᵀA = diag(3, 2). Aᵀb = (2 + 5 + 2, 5 − 2) = (9, 3). x̂ = (9/3, 3/2) = (3, 1.5). Ax̂ = (3, 4.5, 1.5), e = (−1, 0.5, 0.5). Check: Aᵀe = (−1 + 0.5 + 0.5, 0.5 − 0.5) = (0, 0). Option B dono components ko 3 se divide karta hai (AᵀA ka 2 ignore), aur uska Aᵀe = (0, 1) ≠ 0. Option C (AᵀA)⁻¹ bhool jaata hai. Option D sirf pehli do equations exactly solve karta hai aur teesri ko chhod deta hai.

questions.question: b = (4, 7, 1) ka a = (1, 1, 1) ki line par projection p aur squared error ‖b − p‖² kya hai? (Ye sirf intercept wale model ŷ = c ka fit hai.)
questions.explanation: aᵀb = 12, aᵀa = 3, to p = 4 · (1, 1, 1) = (4, 4, 4): intercept-only model mean predict karta hai. e = (0, 3, −3), ‖e‖² = 0 + 9 + 9 = 18. Option A aᵀa se divide karna bhool jaata hai. Option B absolute errors ka sum (0 + 3 + 3) leta hai, squares ka nahi. Option D ‖a‖ = √3 se divide karta hai (12/√3 ≈ 6.93), ‖a‖² se nahi.

questions.question: Points (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 2), (4, 5) par line ŷ = c + mx ka least squares fit karo. Slope m, intercept c aur x = 5 par prediction kya hai?
questions.explanation: x̄ = 2.5, ȳ = 2.5. Sxy = Σ(xᵢ − x̄)(yᵢ − ȳ) = 2.25 + 0.25 − 0.25 + 3.75 = 6, Sxx = 2.25 + 0.25 + 0.25 + 2.25 = 5. m = 6/5 = 1.2, c = ȳ − m x̄ = 2.5 − 3 = −0.5. x = 5 par ŷ = −0.5 + 6 = 5.5. Option A sirf pehle do points se line kheenchta hai, option B pehle aur aakhri point se; dono least squares nahi. Option C c = ȳ le leta hai, m x̄ ghatana bhool gaya.

questions.question: A ke columns a₁ = (1, 2, 3) aur a₂ = (2, 4, 6) hain (a₂ = 2a₁), aur b = (0, 4, 2). x̂ = (1, 0) ek least squares solution hai. Inme se kaunsa x bhi least squares solution hai (same minimum error)?
questions.explanation: Column space sirf a₁ ki line hai. Projection p = (a₁ᵀb / a₁ᵀa₁) a₁ = (14/14) a₁ = (1, 2, 3), jo unique hai. Ax = (x₁ + 2x₂) a₁, to har x jiske liye x₁ + 2x₂ = 1 ho wo solution hai: (−1, 1) par −1 + 2 = 1. Option A par x₁ + 2x₂ = 2, yaani Ax = (2, 4, 6) = 2p. Option C par 3 aur option D par 3. Trap: AᵀA singular hai, to x̂ unique nahi, par har solution ko same p dena chahiye.

weeks.title: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and diagonalisation
weeks.summary: Is week aap characteristic polynomial se eigenvalues nikalna, eigenvectors dhoondhna, matrix ko diagonalise karna, aur Aᵏ jaisi powers ko eigenvalues ki powers se jaldi compute karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Eigenvector aur eigenvalue**: non-zero v jiske liye Av = λv. Matlab A is direction ko ghumata nahi, sirf λ se scale karta hai (λ negative ho to direction ulti). v = 0 kabhi eigenvector nahi hota, par λ = 0 allowed hai (tab A singular hai).

**Characteristic polynomial**: Av = λv ⇔ (A − λI)v = 0 ka non-zero solution ⇔ det(A − λI) = 0. 2 × 2 ke liye ye λ² − (trace)λ + det = 0 ban jaata hai. Har eigenvalue ke liye null space of (A − λI) me eigenvectors milte hain.

**Trace aur determinant**: n × n matrix ke eigenvalues (multiplicity ke saath) ka sum = trace(A) aur product = det(A). Triangular matrix ke eigenvalues seedhe diagonal entries hain. Quick check: 2 × 2 me paaye gaye λ₁, λ₂ ka sum aur product trace aur det se match hone chahiye.
**Eigenvalues of related matrices**: agar Av = λv, to Aᵏv = λᵏv, A⁻¹v = (1/λ)v (λ ≠ 0), (A + cI)v = (λ + c)v, aur (cA)v = cλv. Isliye det(cA) = cⁿ det(A) for n × n, sirf c·det(A) nahi.

**Diagonalisation**: agar A ke n linearly independent eigenvectors hain to A = VΛV⁻¹, jahan V ke columns eigenvectors aur Λ = diag(λᵢ). Distinct eigenvalues hon to eigenvectors guaranteed independent hote hain. Repeated eigenvalue par ho bhi sakta hai (jaise 3I) aur nahi bhi (jaise [[3, 1], [0, 3]], jiska sirf ek eigenvector direction hai: **defective** matrix).

**Powers via eigen-decomposition**: Aᵏ = VΛᵏV⁻¹. Practical tareeka: x ko eigenvectors me likho, x = c₁v₁ + c₂v₂, phir Aᵏx = c₁λ₁ᵏv₁ + c₂λ₂ᵏv₂. Bade k par sabse bada |λ| dominate karta hai; yahi idea power iteration, Markov chains aur PageRank ke peeche hai.

example.problem: Ek fictional app ke users do plans A aur B me hain. Har mahine A ke 90% A me rehte hain aur 10% B me jaate hain; B ke 80% B me rehte hain aur 20% A me jaate hain. Matrix M = [[0.9, 0.2], [0.1, 0.8]], shuru me x₀ = (500, 400). Eigen-decomposition se 2 mahine baad ke users aur long-run split nikalo.
steps: k → ∞ par 0.7ᵏ → 0, to split (600, 300) ki taraf jaata hai.
Answer: **2 mahine baad (551, 349); long run me (600, 300)**, yaani λ = 1 wala eigenvector steady state hai.

mistakes: Har matrix ke eigenvalues diagonal entries maan lena. Ye sirf triangular (ya diagonal) matrix ke liye sach hai; baaki ke liye det(A − λI) = 0 solve karo.
Repeated eigenvalue dekhte hi 'diagonalisable nahi' bol dena. 3I diagonalisable hai; asli test hai ki independent eigenvectors kitne hain.
det(cA) = c·det(A) likhna. n × n matrix ke liye har row c se scale hoti hai, to det(cA) = cⁿ det(A).
revision: Aᵏx = Σ cᵢλᵢᵏvᵢ; bada |λ| dominate karta hai.

questions.question: A = [[2, 5], [0, 3]] ke eigenvalues kya hain?
questions.explanation: Upper triangular matrix ke eigenvalues diagonal entries hain: det(A − λI) = (2 − λ)(3 − λ) ⇒ 2 aur 3. Option A me trace (5) aur det (6) ko hi eigenvalues likh diya; asal me eigenvalues ka sum 5 aur product 6 hai. Off-diagonal 5 ka eigenvalues par koi asar nahi.

questions.question: A = [[4, 1], [2, 3]] aur v = (1, 1). v ke liye kya sahi hai?
questions.explanation: Av = (4 + 1, 2 + 3) = (5, 5) = 5·(1, 1), to v eigenvector hai aur λ = 5. Option B tempting hai kyunki 2 bhi A ka eigenvalue hai (trace 7 − 5 = 2), par uska eigenvector (1, −2) hai, (1, 1) nahi. Option C trace hai.

questions.question: A = [[4, −2], [1, 1]] ke eigenvalues kya hain?
questions.explanation: Trace = 5, det = 4·1 − (−2)(1) = 6. λ² − 5λ + 6 = 0 ⇒ (λ − 2)(λ − 3) = 0 ⇒ 2, 3. Check: 2 + 3 = 5 ✓, 2·3 = 6 ✓. Option A diagonal entries hain, jo sirf triangular matrix me eigenvalues hote. Option B me trace ka sign ulta liya (λ² + 5λ + 6), aur option D me det ka sign ulta (λ² − 5λ − 6).

questions.question: Ek 3 × 3 matrix A ke eigenvalues 1, 2 aur 4 hain. det(2A) kya hai?
questions.explanation: 2A ke eigenvalues 2, 4, 8 hain, product 64. Equivalently det(2A) = 2³·det(A) = 8·8 = 64. Option A (16) ka trap det(2A) = 2·det(A) likhna hai. Option B 2·trace = 2·7 hai, aur option D sirf det(A) hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsi matrix diagonalisable NAHI hai?
questions.explanation: [[3, 1], [0, 3]] ka eigenvalue 3 do baar aata hai, par A − 3I = [[0, 1], [0, 0]] ka null space sirf (1, 0) ki line hai: ek hi independent eigenvector, to defective. Option A tempting hai kyunki usme bhi 3 repeated hai, par 3I already diagonal hai aur har vector eigenvector hai. Option D ke eigenvalues 2, 3 distinct hain, aur option C symmetric hai, dono diagonalisable.

questions.question: A = [[4, −2], [1, 1]] ke eigenpairs hain: λ = 2 with v = (1, 1), aur λ = 3 with v = (2, 1). x = (3, 2) ke liye A⁵x kya hai?
questions.explanation: x = (3, 2) = 1·(1, 1) + 1·(2, 1). To A⁵x = 2⁵(1, 1) + 3⁵(2, 1) = (32, 32) + (486, 243) = (518, 275). Option B me eigenvalues ko galat eigenvectors ke saath jod diya: 3⁵(1, 1) + 2⁵(2, 1). Option C me poore x par sirf 2⁵ lagaya, aur option D me power ki jagah 5 se multiply kiya (λ·5).

questions.question: Ek 2 × 2 matrix ka trace 7 aur determinant 10 hai. Iske eigenvalues kya hain?
questions.explanation: λ² − 7λ + 10 = 0 ⇒ (λ − 2)(λ − 5) = 0, to λ = 2, 5. Check: sum 7 = trace, product 10 = det. Option C ka sum 7 hai par product 12, aur option B ka product 10 hai par sum 11; dono me sirf ek condition match hoti hai. Option A trace aur det ko hi eigenvalues maan leta hai.

questions.question: Ek 2 × 2 matrix A ke eigenvalues 3 aur −2 hain. A² ke eigenvalues kya hain?
questions.explanation: Av = λv ⇒ A²v = λ²v, to eigenvalues 3² = 9 aur (−2)² = 4. Option A minus sign ko square ke baad bhi rakh leta hai. Option C eigenvalues ko 2 se multiply karta hai (ye 2A ke honge). Option D maanta hai ki A² ke eigenvalues same rehte hain.

questions.question: Ek square matrix A ka ek eigenvalue 0 hai. Isse kya pakka pata chalta hai?
options: Us eigenvalue ka eigenvector zero vector hai
questions.explanation: det A = eigenvalues ka product, to ek eigenvalue 0 ho to det A = 0 aur A singular hai (Av = 0 ka non-zero solution hai). Option B galat hai: diag(0, 1) diagonalisable hai. Option C galat hai kyunki eigenvector kabhi zero nahi hota; λ = 0 allowed hai, v = 0 nahi. Option D sirf ek eigenvalue se baaki ke baare me kuch nahi bata sakta.

questions.question: A = [[5, 2], [2, 2]] ka eigenvalue 6 ke liye eigenvector kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: A − 6I = [[−1, 2], [2, −4]], pehli row se −v₁ + 2v₂ = 0 ⇒ v = (2, 1). Check: A(2, 1) = (12, 6) = 6(2, 1). Option B doosre eigenvalue 1 ka eigenvector hai (A(1, −2) = (1, −2)). Options A aur D eigenvectors hi nahi hain: A(1, 2) = (9, 6) aur A(2, −1) = (8, 2), jo un vectors ke multiples nahi.

questions.question: Ek 3 × 3 matrix A ke eigenvalues 2, 4 aur 5 hain. B = 2A⁻¹ + I ke eigenvalues kya hain?
questions.explanation: Same eigenvector v par A⁻¹v = (1/λ)v, to Bv = (2/λ + 1)v. λ = 2, 4, 5 se: 2, 1.5, 1.4. Option A 2A + I ke eigenvalues hai (inverse bhool gaye). Option B me +I chhoot gaya. Option C me 2 ka factor chhoot gaya (A⁻¹ + I).

questions.question: Ek fictional app ke users do plans me hain. Monthly transition matrix M = [[0.7, 0.4], [0.3, 0.6]] hai (column j = plan j se kahan jaate hain). Total 1000 users. Long run me plan A me lagbhag kitne users honge, aur M ka doosra eigenvalue kya hai?
questions.explanation: Steady state λ = 1 ka eigenvector hai: (M − I)v = 0 ⇒ −0.3v₁ + 0.4v₂ = 0 ⇒ v ∝ (4, 3). 1000 users me plan A = 1000 × 4/7 ≈ 571. Doosra eigenvalue = trace − 1 = 1.3 − 1 = 0.3, jiska |λ| < 1 hone se wo component har mahine 0.3 se ghatkar mar jaata hai. Option B ratio ulta kar deta hai (3/7). Option C equal split maan leta hai. Option D me doosra eigenvalue ko diagonal entry 0.7 maan liya.

questions.question: A = [[1, 2], [2, 1]] ke eigenpairs: λ = 3 with v = (1, 1), aur λ = −1 with v = (1, −1). x = (3, 1) ke liye A⁴x kya hai?
questions.explanation: x = 2(1, 1) + 1(1, −1). A⁴x = 2 · 3⁴ (1, 1) + 1 · (−1)⁴ (1, −1) = 162(1, 1) + (1, −1) = (163, 161). Option A maanta hai ki chhota eigenvalue wala term gayab ho jaata hai, par |−1| = 1 hai to wo kabhi nahi marta. Option C (−1)⁴ ko −1 le leta hai. Option D 3⁴ ko seedha x par lagata hai, jaise x khud eigenvector ho.

questions.question: A = [[2, 1, 3], [0, −1, 4], [0, 0, 3]]. det(A² − I) kya hai?
questions.explanation: A upper triangular hai, to eigenvalues 2, −1, 3. A² − I ke eigenvalues λ² − 1: 3, 0, 8. Determinant = product = 3 × 0 × 8 = 0. Option A det A = −6 hai, option B det(A²) = 36 hai, aur option C me det(A²) − 1 kar diya, jo det(A² − I) nahi hota (determinant subtraction par distribute nahi hota).

questions.question: A = [[4, k], [1, 2]]. k ki kis value par A ka repeated eigenvalue hai, aur us k par kya A diagonalisable hai?
options: k = −1; nahi, sirf ek eigenvector direction hai
k = 1; nahi, sirf ek eigenvector direction hai
questions.explanation: Characteristic polynomial λ² − 6λ + (8 − k). Repeated root ke liye discriminant 36 − 4(8 − k) = 0 ⇒ k = −1, aur λ = 3. Tab A − 3I = [[1, −1], [1, −1]] ka rank 1 hai, to null space sirf ek line (1, 1) hai: defective, diagonalisable nahi. Option B repeated eigenvalue ko automatically diagonalisable maan leta hai (ye sirf 3I jaise cases me hota hai). Options A aur D ka k = 1 galat hai: tab discriminant 8 hai aur eigenvalues distinct hain.

weeks.title: Symmetric matrices, quadratic forms and positive definiteness
weeks.summary: Is week aap symmetric matrices ke special properties (real eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenvectors), spectral theorem A = QΛQᵀ, quadratic forms xᵀAx, aur positive definiteness ke tests seekhoge.
concepts: **Symmetric matrix**: A = Aᵀ. ML me ye har jagah milti hai: covariance matrix, Gram matrix XᵀX, Hessian of a smooth function, kernel matrix. Isliye inke properties optimisation aur PCA dono ki neev hain.

**Real eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenvectors**: real symmetric matrix ke saare eigenvalues real hote hain, aur alag eigenvalues ke eigenvectors automatically orthogonal hote hain. Repeated eigenvalue ke eigenspace me bhi orthonormal basis choose kiya ja sakta hai.

**Spectral theorem**: har real symmetric A ko A = QΛQᵀ likh sakte hain, jahan Q orthogonal (QᵀQ = I, columns orthonormal eigenvectors qᵢ) aur Λ diagonal. Equivalent form: A = Σ λᵢ qᵢqᵢᵀ, yaani rank-1 projections ka weighted sum. Q⁻¹ = Qᵀ hone se inverse nikalna bhi free hai.

**Quadratic form**: q(x) = xᵀAx = Σᵢ Σⱼ aᵢⱼxᵢxⱼ. 2 × 2 me xᵀAx = a₁₁x₁² + 2a₁₂x₁x₂ + a₂₂x₂²; cross term par factor 2 aata hai. Ulta, 5x₁² + 4x₁x₂ + 2x₂² ki matrix [[5, 2], [2, 2]] hai (4 ko aadha karke dono off-diagonal me).

**Positive definite (PD)**: xᵀAx > 0 har x ≠ 0 ke liye. Equivalent tests (symmetric A ke liye): saare eigenvalues > 0; saare leading principal minors > 0 (Sylvester); A = RᵀR with R invertible. **Positive semidefinite (PSD)**: ≥ 0, eigenvalues ≥ 0. Covariance matrix aur XᵀX hamesha PSD hote hain, kyunki xᵀ(XᵀX)x = ‖Xx‖² ≥ 0.

**Indefinite**: kuch directions me xᵀAx > 0, kuch me < 0 (eigenvalues ke sign mixed). 2 × 2 me det < 0 ho to matrix pakka indefinite hai. Hessian indefinite ho to critical point saddle hota hai (week 7).

**Rayleigh quotient**: unit vectors ‖x‖ = 1 par xᵀAx ki maximum value λ_max aur minimum λ_min hai, jo top/bottom eigenvectors par milti hai. PCA me yahi result variance maximise karne wali direction deta hai.

example.problem: Quadratic form q(x) = 5x₁² + 4x₁x₂ + 2x₂² ko orthogonally diagonalise karo, batao PD hai ya nahi, aur unit circle ‖x‖ = 1 par q ki maximum value aur direction nikalo.
steps: Matrix: A = [[5, 2], [2, 2]] (cross coefficient 4 ko aadha karke 2).
z = Qᵀx lene par q = 6z₁² + 1·z₂², dono coefficients positive ⇒ PD. Sylvester check: 5 > 0 aur det 6 > 0 ✓.
Unit circle par max = λ_max = 6, direction q₁ = (2, 1)/√5; min = 1, direction q₂.
Answer: **A = QΛQᵀ with Λ = diag(6, 1); PD; max value 6 at x = (2, 1)/√5**.

mistakes: Quadratic form me cross term ka 2 bhool jaana: xᵀAx = a₁₁x₁² + 2a₁₂x₁x₂ + a₂₂x₂², sirf a₁₂x₁x₂ nahi.
Sirf diagonal entries positive dekh kar PD bol dena. [[1, 2], [2, 1]] ki diagonal positive hai par eigenvalues 3 aur −1 hain, to indefinite.
PD aur PSD ko mix karna: det = 0 wali matrix (jaise [[1, 2], [2, 4]]) PSD hai par PD nahi, kyunki kisi non-zero x par xᵀAx = 0 hota hai.
revision: Spectral theorem: A = QΛQᵀ = Σ λᵢqᵢqᵢᵀ.
PD ⇔ all λ > 0 ⇔ all leading minors > 0.
XᵀX aur covariance matrix hamesha PSD.

questions.question: Real symmetric matrix A ke baare me kaunsa statement HAMESHA sahi hai?
options: A ke saare eigenvalues positive hote hain
Alag eigenvalues ke eigenvectors orthogonal hote hain
A ke eigenvalues uski diagonal entries hote hain
questions.explanation: Spectral theorem ka hissa: real symmetric matrix ke distinct eigenvalues ke eigenvectors orthogonal hote hain (aur saare eigenvalues real hote hain). Option B ka trap 'real' ko 'positive' samajhna hai; [[1, 2], [2, 1]] ka eigenvalue −1 hai. Option A galat: [[1, 1], [1, 1]] symmetric hai par singular. Option D sirf triangular/diagonal matrix ke liye sach hai.

questions.question: A = [[2, 1], [1, 2]] ke eigenvalues aur ek orthonormal eigenvector set kya hai?
questions.explanation: Trace 4, det 3 ⇒ λ² − 4λ + 3 = 0 ⇒ 3, 1. A(1, 1) = (3, 3) aur A(1, −1) = (1, −1); dono ko √2 se normalise karo, aur ye orthogonal hain. Option A diagonal entries ko eigenvalues maan leta hai. Option C ke vectors orthogonal nahi aur (1, 0) eigenvector bhi nahi (A(1, 0) = (2, 1)). Option D me trace aur det ko eigenvalues likh diya.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsi matrix positive definite hai?
questions.explanation: Sylvester test: [[2, −1], [−1, 2]] ke liye 2 > 0 aur det = 4 − 1 = 3 > 0, eigenvalues 3 aur 1 ⇒ PD. Option A ki diagonal positive hai par det = 1 − 4 = −3 < 0 ⇒ indefinite (yahi sabse bada trap hai). Option B ka det 0 hai ⇒ sirf PSD (x = (2, −1) par xᵀAx = 0). Option C ka ek eigenvalue −1 hai.

questions.question: A = [[3, 1], [1, 2]] aur x = (1, −2). Quadratic form xᵀAx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: xᵀAx = 3x₁² + 2·1·x₁x₂ + 2x₂² = 3(1) + 2(1)(−2) + 2(4) = 3 − 4 + 8 = 7. Ya Ax = (3 − 2, 1 − 4) = (1, −3), phir x · Ax = 1 + 6 = 7. Option B me cross term ka factor 2 bhool gaye (3 − 2 + 8). Option C me cross term poora chhod diya (3 + 8), aur option D me uska sign + le liya (3 + 4 + 8).

questions.question: Ek symmetric 2 × 2 matrix ke eigenpairs hain: λ₁ = 4 with q₁ = (1, 1)/√2, aur λ₂ = 2 with q₂ = (1, −1)/√2. A = λ₁q₁q₁ᵀ + λ₂q₂q₂ᵀ kya hai?
questions.explanation: q₁q₁ᵀ = ½[[1, 1], [1, 1]], q₂q₂ᵀ = ½[[1, −1], [−1, 1]]. A = 2[[1, 1], [1, 1]] + [[1, −1], [−1, 1]] = [[3, 1], [1, 3]]. Check: trace 6 = 4 + 2, det 8 = 4·2 ✓. Option A sirf Λ hai (Q ko ignore kiya). Option D me ½ factor (normalisation √2 ka square) bhool gaye, aur option C me eigenvalues eigenvectors ke saath swap ho gaye.

questions.question: A = [[2, 1, 0], [1, 2, 1], [0, 1, k]]. k ki kis range ke liye A positive definite hai?
questions.explanation: Leading principal minors: 2 > 0; det [[2, 1], [1, 2]] = 3 > 0; det A = 2(2k − 1) − 1(k − 0) + 0 = 3k − 2. PD ke liye 3k − 2 > 0 ⇒ k > 2/3. Option B me cofactor expansion ka doosra term −1·(k) chhoot gaya (sirf 2(2k − 1) > 0). Option A ka trap sirf diagonal entry positive dekhna hai. Option D me k = 2/3 par det = 0, matrix sirf PSD hoti hai.

questions.question: Quadratic form q(x) = 3x₁² − 6x₁x₂ + x₂² ki symmetric matrix A (q = xᵀAx) kya hai?
questions.explanation: xᵀAx me cross term 2a₁₂x₁x₂ hai, to 2a₁₂ = −6 ⇒ a₁₂ = a₂₁ = −3. Option B cross coefficient ko aadha karna bhool jaata hai (ye 3x₁² − 12x₁x₂ + x₂² deta). Option C same q deta hai par symmetric nahi hai, jabki question symmetric matrix maang raha hai. Option D me sign galat hai.

questions.question: Real symmetric A ke spectral decomposition A = QΛQᵀ me Q ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: Q ka determinant hamesha 0 hota hai
Q ke columns A ki rows hoti hain
questions.explanation: Q ke columns orthonormal eigenvectors hain, isliye QᵀQ = I aur inverse bas transpose hai. Option A galat hai: orthogonal matrix ka symmetric hona zaroori nahi (jaise rotation). Option B galat hai kyunki orthogonal Q ka det ±1 hota hai, kabhi 0 nahi. Option D eigenvectors ko A ki rows se confuse karta hai.

questions.question: Kisi bhi real matrix X ke liye XᵀX ke baare me kya hamesha sahi hai?
options: XᵀX ke eigenvalues negative ho sakte hain
questions.explanation: vᵀ(XᵀX)v = ‖Xv‖² ≥ 0 har v ke liye, aur (XᵀX)ᵀ = XᵀX, to ye symmetric PSD hai. Option A tabhi sahi hai jab X ke columns independent hon; warna kisi v ≠ 0 par Xv = 0 hota hai. Options C aur D isi wajah se galat hain: XᵀX hamesha symmetric hai aur eigenvalues ≥ 0.

questions.question: A = [[k, 2], [2, 3]]. k ki kis range ke liye A positive definite hai?
questions.explanation: Sylvester: leading minors k > 0 aur det = 3k − 4 > 0 ⇒ k > 4/3 (jo k > 0 ko bhi cover karta hai). Option A sirf pehla minor check karta hai; k = 1 par det = −1 < 0 aur A indefinite hai. Option B sufficient hai par poori range nahi deta. Option C fraction ulta kar deta hai.

questions.question: A = [[3, 2], [2, 0]]. Unit vectors ‖x‖ = 1 par xᵀAx ki maximum aur minimum value kya hai, aur A kis type ki hai?
questions.explanation: Trace 3, det −4 ⇒ λ² − 3λ − 4 = 0 ⇒ λ = 4, −1. Rayleigh quotient: max = λ_max = 4, min = λ_min = −1. Eigenvalues ke sign mixed hain (det < 0), to A indefinite hai. Option B diagonal entries ko hi extremes maan leta hai. Option C eigenvalue ka sign galat leta hai. Option D me max = 3 + 2 = 5 jod diya.

questions.question: A = [[5, 3], [3, 5]] ke eigenpairs: λ₁ = 8 with q₁ = (1, 1)/√2, λ₂ = 2 with q₂ = (1, −1)/√2. Spectral form A³ = λ₁³q₁q₁ᵀ + λ₂³q₂q₂ᵀ se A³ kya hai?
questions.explanation: q₁q₁ᵀ = ½[[1, 1], [1, 1]], q₂q₂ᵀ = ½[[1, −1], [−1, 1]]. A³ = 512 · ½[[1, 1], [1, 1]] + 8 · ½[[1, −1], [−1, 1]] = [[256 + 4, 256 − 4], [256 − 4, 256 + 4]] = [[260, 252], [252, 260]]. Option A har entry ko alag se cube karta hai, jo matrix power nahi hai. Option C qqᵀ ka ½ bhool jaata hai. Option D λ₂ wale term ka sign ulta kar deta hai.

questions.question: Quadratic form q(x, y, z) = x² + 2y² + 3z² + 2xy + 2yz ko symmetric matrix me likhkar classify karo.
questions.explanation: Cross terms aadhe karke: A = [[1, 1, 0], [1, 2, 1], [0, 1, 3]]. Minors: 1; 1·2 − 1·1 = 1; det = 1(6 − 1) − 1(3 − 0) + 0 = 2. Sab positive ⇒ PD. Option C cross coefficients ko aadha nahi karta (A = [[1, 2, 0], [2, 2, 2], [0, 2, 3]] lene par minors 1, −2, −10 aate hain), yahi main trap hai. Option D sirf diagonal ke products leta hai. Option B ka det galat hai.

questions.question: Unit vectors ‖x‖ = 1 par q(x) = 2x₁² + 4x₁x₂ + 5x₂² ki maximum value kya hai aur kis direction me milti hai?
questions.explanation: Symmetric matrix A = [[2, 2], [2, 5]] (cross term 4 ka aadha). Trace 7, det 6 ⇒ λ = 6, 1. Max = λ_max = 6. λ = 6 ke liye (A − 6I) ki pehli row −4v₁ + 2v₂ = 0 ⇒ v ∝ (1, 2). Option D me value sahi hai par direction λ = 1 wala eigenvector hai (wahan q = 1). Option B cross term ko aadha nahi karta ([[2, 4], [4, 5]] lena). Option A sirf sabse badi diagonal entry dekhta hai.

questions.question: Centered data ki covariance matrix C = [[4, 2], [2, 1]] hai. Combination z = x₁ − 2x₂ ka variance wᵀCw (w = (1, −2)) kya hai, aur iska C ke baare me kya matlab hai?
options: Var = 0; C PSD hai par PD nahi
questions.explanation: wᵀCw = 4(1)² + 2 · 2 · (1)(−2) + 1 · (−2)² = 4 − 8 + 4 = 0. Ek non-zero w par variance 0 hai, to C PD nahi; det C = 4 − 4 = 0 bhi yahi kehta hai (eigenvalues 5 aur 0). Matlab data ek line x₁ = 2x₂ par pada hai. Option A cross term chhod deta hai (4 + 4), option B cross term ko 2 se multiply nahi karta (4 − 4 + 4), aur option C w ka sign galat leta hai (w = (1, 2) par 16).

weeks.title: Singular value decomposition and principal component analysis
weeks.summary: Is week aap kisi bhi matrix ka SVD A = UΣVᵀ samajhna, singular values ko AᵀA ke eigenvalues se nikalna, best low-rank approximation banana, aur PCA se data ke variance ko kam dimensions me pakadna seekhoge.
concepts: **SVD**: har m × n real matrix A = UΣVᵀ likhi ja sakti hai, jahan U (m × m) aur V (n × n) orthogonal hain aur Σ diagonal hai with σ₁ ≥ σ₂ ≥ … ≥ 0. Eigen-decomposition ke ulat, SVD rectangular aur non-symmetric matrices ke liye bhi hamesha exist karta hai.

**Singular values kahan se aate hain**: AᵀA = VΣᵀΣVᵀ, to V ke columns AᵀA ke eigenvectors hain aur σᵢ = √(AᵀA ke eigenvalues). Isi tarah U ke columns AAᵀ ke eigenvectors hain, aur uᵢ = Avᵢ / σᵢ. Singular values kabhi negative nahi hote; rank(A) = non-zero σ ki count.
**Outer-product form**: A = Σᵢ σᵢuᵢvᵢᵀ. Har term ek rank-1 matrix hai, aur σᵢ batata hai ki wo term kitna important hai.
**Best low-rank approximation (Eckart–Young)**: pehle k terms Aₖ = Σᵢ≤ₖ σᵢuᵢvᵢᵀ rank-k matrices me A ke sabse kareeb hain. Error: ‖A − Aₖ‖_F² = σ²ₖ₊₁ + … + σ²ᵣ aur spectral norm ‖A − Aₖ‖₂ = σₖ₊₁.

**Image compression idea**: m × n grayscale image ko rank k par rakhne ke liye k(m + n + 1) numbers chahiye (k vectors uᵢ, k vectors vᵢ, k singular values) jabki full image me mn. Jab singular values tezi se girte hain, chhota k bhi achhi quality deta hai.

**PCA**: data X (n × d) ko pehle center karo (har column ka mean ghatao). Covariance C = (1/n) XᵀX symmetric PSD hai. Uske eigenvectors principal directions hain aur eigenvalue λᵢ us direction me variance hai. Pehla PC wo unit direction hai jo projected variance maximise karta hai (Rayleigh quotient).

**Variance explained**: k components ka ratio = (λ₁ + … + λₖ) / (λ₁ + … + λ_d). Ye ratio 1/n ya 1/(n − 1) normalisation par depend nahi karta, kyunki dono sab eigenvalues ko same factor se scale karte hain.

**PCA via SVD**: centered X = UΣVᵀ ho to principal directions V ke columns hain aur covariance eigenvalues λᵢ = σᵢ²/n. Practice me libraries PCA isi tarah SVD se compute karti hain, kyunki XᵀX banana numerically kam stable hai.

example.problem: A = [[2, 0], [0, 1], [2, 0]] (3 × 2) ka SVD nikalo aur best rank-1 approximation ka Frobenius error batao.
steps: V ke columns: v₁ = (1, 0), v₂ = (0, 1) (AᵀA already diagonal hai).
u₁ = Av₁/σ₁ = (2, 0, 2)/(2√2) = (1, 0, 1)/√2; u₂ = Av₂/σ₂ = (0, 1, 0). Teesra u₃ = (1, 0, −1)/√2 sirf U ko complete karta hai.

mistakes: Singular values ko A ke eigenvalues samajhna. [[2, 0], [0, −3]] ke eigenvalues 2, −3 hain par singular values 3, 2 hain (hamesha non-negative, decreasing order).
PCA se pehle data center na karna. Bina centering ke pehla component aksar mean ki taraf point karta hai, variance ki taraf nahi.
Compression storage me sirf k(m + n) ginna aur k singular values bhool jaana, ya ulta poori U aur V (m² + n²) gin lena.
revision: σᵢ² = eigenvalues of AᵀA; uᵢ = Avᵢ/σᵢ.
PCA: centered covariance ke eigenvectors; λᵢ = variance along PCᵢ.
Explained ratio = Σ top-k λ / Σ all λ.

questions.question: Ek matrix A ke liye AᵀA ke eigenvalues 9 aur 4 hain. A ke singular values kya hain?
questions.explanation: σᵢ = √(AᵀA ke eigenvalues) = √9, √4 = 3, 2. Option A ka trap AᵀA ke eigenvalues ko hi singular values maan lena hai; wo σ² hain. Option B me square kar diya jabki square root lena tha.

questions.question: 3 features wale centered data ki covariance matrix ke eigenvalues 6, 3 aur 1 hain. Pehle do principal components kitna variance explain karte hain?
questions.explanation: Total variance = 6 + 3 + 1 = 10. Pehle do: (6 + 3)/10 = 90%. Option A sirf pehle PC ka hissa (6/10) hai. Option C me 6/9 liya, yaani denominator me sirf pehle do eigenvalues rakhe; ratio hamesha total variance se banta hai.

questions.question: A = [[2, 0], [0, −3]] ke singular values (decreasing order me) kya hain?
questions.explanation: AᵀA = [[4, 0], [0, 9]], eigenvalues 9, 4 ⇒ σ = 3, 2. Sign U ke ek column me chala jaata hai (v₁ = e₂, u₁ = −e₂, kyunki Ae₂ = 3·(−e₂)), singular values hamesha ≥ 0 hote hain. Option B aur D A ke eigenvalues hain, jo symmetric matrix me bhi negative ho sakte hain; option C σ² hai.

questions.question: Ek matrix ke singular values 5, 3 aur 1 hain. Best rank-1 approximation A₁ ke liye squared Frobenius error ‖A − A₁‖_F² kya hai?
questions.explanation: Eckart–Young: ‖A − A₁‖_F² = σ₂² + σ₃² = 9 + 1 = 10. Option A sirf σ₂² hai, jo spectral-norm error (σ₂ = 3) ka square hai, Frobenius ka nahi. Option D me singular values ko square kiye bina jod diya (3 + 1).

questions.question: Ek 100 × 80 grayscale image ko SVD se rank 10 par store karna hai (10 left vectors, 10 right vectors, 10 singular values). Kitne numbers store karne padenge?
questions.explanation: Rank k ke liye k(m + n + 1) = 10(100 + 80 + 1) = 1810, jo full image ke 8000 numbers ka lagbhag 23% hai. Option B me 10 singular values bhool gaye. Option C original image ka size hai, aur option D sirf right vectors (10 × 80) hai.

questions.question: Chaar centered data points hain: (2, 1), (−2, −1), (1, 2), (−1, −2). Pehla principal component kis direction me hai aur wo kitna variance explain karta hai?
questions.explanation: C = (1/4)XᵀX = [[2.5, 2], [2, 2.5]]. Eigenvalues 2.5 ± 2 = 4.5 aur 0.5; λ = 4.5 ka eigenvector (1, 1)/√2. Ratio 4.5/5 = 90% (1/(n − 1) lene par eigenvalues 6 aur 2/3 aate hain, ratio phir bhi 90%). Option A chhote eigenvalue ka eigenvector hai. Option C me ek original axis ka variance 2.5/5 le liya. Option D sirf pehle data point ki direction hai, variance-maximising direction nahi.

questions.question: Ek 4 × 5 matrix ke singular values 7, 2, 0, 0 hain. Iska rank kya hai?
questions.explanation: Rank = non-zero singular values ki count = 2. Option A matrix ki rows ya singular values ki total count hai. Option C sabse bada singular value hai aur option D unka sum; dono rank nahi batate.

questions.question: Singular value decomposition A = UΣVᵀ kin matrices ke liye hamesha exist karta hai?
questions.explanation: SVD har real matrix ka hota hai, rectangular aur singular bhi. Options A, B aur D eigen-decomposition (ya inverse) ki conditions ko SVD par laga dete hain; SVD ka fayda hi ye hai ki use in restrictions ki zaroorat nahi.

questions.question: PCA lagane se pehle data matrix X ke saath kaunsa step zaroori hai?
options: Har feature ka mean ghatakar data center karna
Rows ko kisi feature ke hisaab se sort karna
Har feature ko uske maximum se multiply karna
questions.explanation: Covariance C = (1/n)XᵀX tabhi sahi hai jab har column ka mean 0 ho; bina centering ke pehla PC aksar sirf mean ki direction pakad leta hai. Option B se kuch nahi badalta (rows ka order covariance par asar nahi karta). Options C aur D data ko bigaadte hain aur PCA ka hissa nahi hain.

questions.question: n = 50 points ke centered data X ke singular values 10 aur 5 hain. Covariance C = (1/n)XᵀX ke eigenvalues aur pehle PC ka variance explained kya hai?
questions.explanation: λᵢ = σᵢ²/n: 100/50 = 2 aur 25/50 = 0.5. Variance explained = 2/2.5 = 80%. Option A singular values ko hi eigenvalues maan leta hai aur ratio σ se nikalta hai (10/15). Option B ratio galat leta hai, σ² ki jagah σ. Option C ka ratio sahi hai par n se divide karna bhool gaya.

questions.question: Ek matrix A ke singular values 6, 4, 2, 1 hain. Best rank-2 approximation A₂ ke liye spectral norm error ‖A − A₂‖₂ aur squared Frobenius error ‖A − A₂‖_F² kya hain?
questions.explanation: Eckart–Young: ‖A − A₂‖₂ = σ₃ = 2 aur ‖A − A₂‖_F² = σ₃² + σ₄² = 4 + 1 = 5. Option A spectral error ke liye aakhri σ le leta hai. Option C bache hue σ ka sum leta hai, squares ka nahi. Option D rakhe gaye hisse ka σ₁² + σ₂² = 52 deta hai, jo error nahi hai.

questions.question: A = [[3, 0], [4, 5]] ke singular values kya hain?
questions.explanation: AᵀA = [[9 + 16, 20], [20, 25]] = [[25, 20], [20, 25]], eigenvalues 25 ± 20 = 45 aur 5. σ = √45 ≈ 6.708 aur √5 ≈ 2.236. Check: σ₁σ₂ = √225 = 15 = |det A|. Option A A ke eigenvalues (diagonal) hain; non-symmetric matrix ke liye ye singular values nahi hote. Option B square root bhool jaata hai. Option D rows ke norms (√41 ≈ 6.403 aur 3) le leta hai.

questions.question: Ek 200 × 150 grayscale image ko rank-k SVD (k left vectors, k right vectors, k singular values) se store karna hai, aur storage original ke 10% se kam honi chahiye. Sabse bada allowed k kya hai?
questions.explanation: Original = 200 × 150 = 30000 numbers, 10% = 3000. Rank k ke liye k(200 + 150 + 1) = 351k < 3000 ⇒ k < 8.55, to k = 8 (351 × 8 = 2808, jabki k = 9 par 3159 > 3000). Option B 8.55 ko upar round kar deta hai. Option C 10% condition bhool jaata hai (30000/351). Option D sirf 3000/200 karta hai, poore storage formula ke bina.

questions.question: Chaar centered points: (4, 2), (−4, −2), (1, −2), (−1, 2). Covariance (1/n) use karke pehla principal component aur uska variance explained kya hai?
questions.explanation: Σx² = 34, Σy² = 16, Σxy = 8 + 8 − 2 − 2 = 12, to C = [[8.5, 3], [3, 4]]. Trace 12.5, det 34 − 9 = 25 ⇒ λ = 10, 2.5. λ = 10 ke liye −1.5v₁ + 3v₂ = 0 ⇒ v ∝ (2, 1). Variance explained = 10/12.5 = 80%. Option C ka ratio sahi hai par direction ke components ulte hain. Option A sirf x-axis ka variance (8.5/12.5) leta hai, aur option D (1, 1) direction maan leta hai jiska variance 9.25 hai, maximum nahi.

questions.question: Ek dataset ka mean μ = (2, 1) aur pehla PC u = (0.6, 0.8) hai. Raw point x = (7, 1) ko sirf 1 PC se represent kiya. Score z = uᵀ(x − μ) aur squared reconstruction error ‖(x − μ) − zu‖² kya hain?
questions.explanation: Centered point x − μ = (5, 0). z = 0.6 × 5 + 0.8 × 0 = 3. Reconstruction zu = (1.8, 2.4), error vector (3.2, −2.4), squared error = 10.24 + 5.76 = 16 (shortcut: ‖x − μ‖² − z² = 25 − 9). Option A centering bhool jaata hai (z = uᵀx = 5). weeks.title: Unconstrained optimisation: gradient descent and Newton's method
weeks.summary: Is week aap critical points ko Hessian se classify karna, gradient descent ka update aur step size ka asar samajhna, aur Newton's method ke curvature-based step ko compare karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Training = optimisation**: ML model fit karne ka matlab hai loss L(w) ko w par minimise karna. Unconstrained problem me w pe koi restriction nahi; x* local minimum hai agar uske aas-paas koi point usse chhota value nahi deta, aur global agar poore domain me koi nahi.

**First-order condition**: differentiable f ke interior local minimum par ∇f(x*) = 0 (stationary/critical point). Ye necessary hai, sufficient nahi: maxima aur saddle points par bhi gradient zero hota hai.

**Second-order conditions**: critical point par Hessian H dekho. H positive definite ⇒ strict local minimum; negative definite ⇒ local maximum; indefinite (mixed-sign eigenvalues) ⇒ saddle point; semidefinite (koi eigenvalue 0) ⇒ test inconclusive. 2 × 2 shortcut: det H < 0 ⇒ saddle; det H > 0 aur H₁₁ > 0 ⇒ minimum.

**Gradient descent**: xₖ₊₁ = xₖ − η∇f(xₖ). −∇f local steepest descent direction hai aur η (learning rate) step ki length control karta hai. Large datasets par gradient ko mini-batch se estimate karna stochastic gradient descent (SGD) hai.

**Step size aur convergence**: quadratic f(x) = ½xᵀHx ke liye GD har eigen-direction ko factor (1 − ηλᵢ) se multiply karta hai. Convergence ke liye |1 − ηλᵢ| < 1 sab i ke liye, yaani 0 < η < 2/λ_max. Bahut chhota η: slow; 1/λ_max aur 2/λ_max ke beech: oscillate karke converge; 2/λ_max se bada: diverge. λ_max/λ_min (condition number) bada ho to GD zig-zag karta hai.

**Newton's method**: second-order Taylor model ko minimise karo: xₖ₊₁ = xₖ − H⁻¹∇f(xₖ). Ye curvature ke hisaab se har direction ko alag scale karta hai, isliye quadratic function ka minimum ek hi step me mil jaata hai aur minimum ke paas convergence quadratic (bahut tez) hoti hai. Cost: Hessian banana aur solve karna O(d³), isliye bade models me quasi-Newton ya first-order methods use hote hain.

**Practical checks**: loss har iteration me ghat raha hai ya nahi plot karo; badh raha ho to η kam karo. Features ko standardise karne se Hessian ka condition number sudharta hai aur GD tez chalta hai.

example.problem: f(x, y) = x² + 4y², start (4, 1). Gradient descent with η = 0.1 ke do steps lo, sabse bada stable η batao, aur Newton ka ek step compare karo.
steps: Step 1: (3.2, 0.2). Step 2: (2.56, 0.04). y-direction (curvature 8) tez shrink hoti hai, x-direction (curvature 2) dheere.

Newton: H⁻¹∇f = (2x/2, 8y/8) = (x, y), to (4, 1) − (4, 1) = (0, 0), exact minimum ek step me.
Answer: **GD after 2 steps: (2.56, 0.04); η < 0.25 required; Newton reaches (0, 0) in one step**.

for step in range(2):

Update me sign galat lagana: x − η∇f sahi hai, x + η∇f gradient ascent hai jo loss badhata hai.
Learning rate 'jitna bada utna tez' samajhna. η > 2/λ_max par iterations diverge karti hain; loss curve ko monitor karo.

questions.question: f(x) = x² − 4x par gradient descent x₀ = 0 aur learning rate η = 0.25 se chalaya. x₁ kya hai?
